source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Pink disease, caused by the fungus Erythricium salmonicolor, produces a distinctive pink to salmon-colored fungal growth on the bark of branches and the trunk, usually starting where two branches fork or where bark has been damaged, and can girdle and kill the affected branch if not caught early. It is favored by high humidity and is more common in densely planted or poorly pruned orchards where air circulation through the canopy is limited. General control approach: prune out and destroy affected branches, cutting well back into clean wood below the visible pink growth, improve canopy air circulation through appropriate pruning and spacing, and treat cut surfaces and nearby healthy bark with fungicide paste as a precaution.
